pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all rows are 0 and 2 is rejected.
'AC-2' test asserts ★ only on the starred item; src/index.js item().
'AC-3' stars 3 then 1 and expects id order [First, Third] with 200.
'AC-4' checks / and ?show=all both return all items in id order.

The commit 'Follow-up edits' changed AC-5 from "All items" to "Most items" after the go, with no decision recording the owner's call. The code and the test use "All items", which matches neither the edited AC-5 nor a recorded decision. The spec now contradicts itself (AC-5 says "Most items", the core flow and States table say "All items").
'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty and __proto__; Object.hasOwn guards the prototype case.
traffic/routes.json contains "/?show=starred"; 'AC-7' test asserts it. The checker was updated to accept a query, with tests in tests/traffic-config.test.sh.

findings.what: Commit c1138c2 'Follow-up edits' changed acceptance item AC-5 from "All items" to "Most items" after the owner's go (2026-10-12). No decision in the spec records the owner's call or its date. The spec now contradicts its own core flow and States table, which say "All items". The implementation and test use "All items", so they no longer match AC-5 as written.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-5 edit to "All items". If the owner really wants "Most items", record a dated decision, then change the code, the tests, the flow and the States table together.

findings.what: The 'No starred items' state row lists a link to All items, but its test never checks that link. A regression that dropped or mislinked the nav in the empty starred view would still pass. The 'Empty table' and 'Starred view' tests also never check the link target.
findings.fix: In the 'No starred items' test, assert the page contains 'All items'.

findings.what: The body says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but the 'Follow-up edits' commit edited acceptance item AC-5 after the go.
findings.fix: Disclose the AC-5 change in the PR body, or revert it.

lenses.note: The spec exists. AC-5 was altered after the go without a recorded decision.
AC-5 is unmet and was edited late. The other items and all four state rows have tests; the No starred items row is only partly checked.
I did not run the tests; CI covers them. They assert behaviour. The traffic fake's change is disclosed and needed. The link in the No starred items state is untested.
The README mentions ?show=starred. The spec is self-contradictory on the link text.
src/index.js looks correct. Object.hasOwn blocks prototype keys, and the SQL is static. The routes regex now allows any non-space, non-# characters after the path, which is acceptable.
Output is escaped. The show value is only looked up in a fixed map and never interpolated. No planted instructions found.
The page is bare HTML with a single link; there is no styling or UI component files in the diff.
No UI flow beyond a plain link; no screenshots or browser were available.
The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false because of the AC-5 edit.
